question.text: Which among the following compounds is most acidic?

options.text: <math><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></math>

<math><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></math>

solution.text: Any electron withdrawing substituent (having -I effect) stabilises the anion by dispersing the negative charge and therefore, increases the acidity. Chlorine is an electron withdrawing group present at minimum distance.
